doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Songwriting craft: titles, puzzles and topical songs
summary: Lyrics are like crossword puzzles; he starts from a title, and dislikes writing topical material.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It must have been like a little puzzle trying to put that whole lyric together.
Well I think just about all songs are that way. I’ve often thought of them as that way. Always it’s very much like a crossword puzzle of some kind, yeah.
And I think I’ve read that you said the title is half the battle sometimes.

Well the title is the springboard that I work off of, absolutely. I always try to find a title. If there’s a melody given me I always try to find a title in it, the first thing. Now where is the title going to be? What part of the melody will bear that weight? And then when you find a title that often given an idea as to what the attitude of the song might be, depending on the title, and it gives you an idea of who might be singing it or what the point of view might be. It also gives you an idea of how to pay the lyric off. It’s nice and neat to find a title that will pay itself off in some way, that will fulfill itself by the end of the song. And in those ways finding a title is very helpful, especially in beginning a song, giving you a start.
That inspiration, do you find yourself looking at current events or just social things?

No I don’t. I don’t. I’ve had, as a professional songwriter I’ve been asked and commissioned, hired, to write topical songs sometimes. So some of the songs I’ve written are indeed topical. But I don’t enjoy writing them because they fall into a domain that I’m not that much interested in, it’s material, as opposed to songs. It’s material. And I had to write a lot of topical things when I worked for that television show. It’s demanding work and well it was demanding because it was television.
